items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The bass player with the Jeeter-Pillar group was Carl Pruitt who was well known around the Apple.

ctx.x: We played some camps far away on some other islands which included Clark Field Batan and Subic Bay. When we returned to Manila the 2nd of January 1946, we were billeted in a large camp which had formally been occupied by a military service known as Sea Bees. There seemed to be hundreds of U.S.O. shows there, and the camp was jumping. We were about five miles from Manila but there were plenty of little shops near the camp where whisky was sold and whisky was plentiful and cheap. Curby and I became drinking buddies…

There was gambling in the upstairs recreation room and jam sessions downstairs. Jessie Stone, the composer of Idaho had a band which included Franz Jackson on tenor and Louis Bacon on trumpet, Otis Johnson, an ex-Luis Russell trumpeter and Fess Williams' son Rudy were with the group. The Jeeter-Pillar orchestra of St.Louis fame were there, and one of the trumpet players was a fine solo man named Sam Massenberg who had been a member of the Savoy Sultans. The bass player with the Jeeter-Pillar group was Carl Pruitt…

There were two Broadway hit shows with lots of girls at the camp. One was "Gingham Girl" and the other was "Meet me at the Astor". Many of the actos were show people that had come out of forced retirement and were very happy because the pay was good and the food was not bad except on Sundays. And the only thing bad about food that day or any Philippine holiday was the chicken.
